newsitem.title: FINLAND: OVERALL PAY DEAL WOULD BE GOOD BUT DIFFICULT - AKAVA.
newsitem.headline: OVERALL PAY DEAL WOULD BE GOOD BUT DIFFICULT - AKAVA.

text.p: A pay deal covering all branches would be good but reaching one will be clearly harder now compared to 1995, the Confederation of Unions for Academic Professionals in Finland (Akava) said on Tuesday.

"Reaching a broad and binding pay deal in the next round of talks will be significantly more difficult than in autumn 1995," Akava chairman Mikko Viitasalo said in a statement with a summary of his speech to Akava's union meeting.
"But my view is that a comprehensive incomes settlement would benefit Finland's economic development," he added.
In a separate statement, Akava public sector negotiation head Erkki Kangasniemi said a comprehensive deal could not be reached unless all main unions joined it.
"If a single major sector remains outside a deal, a comprehensive settlement can be forgotten right away," he said.
The current two-year deal with moderate pay hikes had proved better than expected for people with jobs, while the main disappointment was weak employment, he said.
Viitasalo said income taxes should still be lowered and the income distribution should be changed to favour the well-educated.
